No internet permission at all — the app physically cannot send data anywhere.
The accessibility permission only watches for the two volume keys. Screen contents are never read.
The volume permission exists solely to undo the single volume step the shortcut causes.
The vibration permission drives the confirmation buzz, and nothing else.
Switch the torch on and off with the volume keys.

NightTorch watches for both volume keys being pressed together, so you can switch the torch on and off without unlocking your phone, finding the right app, or aiming for an on-screen button. That makes the torch usable one-handed, in the dark, and without looking at the screen.

Watching for key presses is the only way an app can react to the volume keys while your phone is locked or another app is open, which is why this permission is needed.

NightTorch does not read the contents of your screen, and it has no internet permission, so it cannot send anything anywhere. Single volume presses keep working exactly as normal.
Press both volume keys together to switch the torch on or off, even when your phone is locked.

At night it comes on dim, so it does not dazzle you at 3am. During the day it comes on bright. You choose the hours.
No internet permission, so the app cannot send anything anywhere. You can verify that in Android\'s own permission list.
Watching for the volume keys while your phone is locked or another app is open needs Android\'s accessibility permission. That is the only way any app can do it.

The next screen says NightTorch wants to "view and control your screen". That warning is the same for every accessibility service and Android cannot tailor it.\n\nNightTorch asks only for key presses. It does not request permission to read screen content, and the code is open if you want to check.
Waiting for the service to be switched on…

Android blocks accessibility settings for apps installed outside an app store. To allow it:

1. Open Settings, then Apps, then NightTorch
2. Tap ⋮ in the top right
3. Choose "Allow restricted settings"

Then come back and try again.
These are already set to sensible defaults. Change them now or later — everything here is on the main screen too.
